item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Hi again EnderDragon101,

It looks like you've cleared up alot of the details but honestly, the overall concept hasn't changed much. I still feel it's too ambitious and am unsure how the various sub-plots tie-in together to make a coherent narrative.

For now, unless you make significant revisions to the concept, I'm going to have to pass on the greenlight. By all means, continue to reach out to other reviewers for a second opinion. In the worst case scenario, you could also just prove all of us wrong and write out the draft and post a successful article on the mainlist on your own, though we'd always caution against doing that without getting any feedback.

For now, all the best with the writing!

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: since when did the GOC get space cannons and what do you mean by an alien ship falling from the sky.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is an alien ship that was shot down by the GOC and crashed 20 miles west of San Francisco, pieces of the SCP-XXXX was too badly damaged to know the original shape or size of it.

The name Galactic.Co also appears on multiple occasions on walls and windows, the majority of the SCP-XXXX is a core fueled by large glass containers with a very small amount of SCP-XXXX-2, known as gravitonium.

SCP-XXXX-1 is the Survivors of the incident and appears to be a combination of a human and a orca, they are strong, intelligent and can swim very fast, they were discovered in Hawaii existing their escape pods with a few of them injured, because of the GOC they are stuck here with no way for them to contact their home world.

+ show block
– hide block

They claimed that they’re from the other side of the galaxy testing some new form of hyper drive from Galactic.Co, the only problem is that it needs larger amounts of SCP-XXXX-2, they thought that there’s enough to go here and back but when they got here, the glass container was almost completely empty.

As for project space cannon, the GOC was building it after the interaction with SCP-2845, knowing that SCP-2845 came from space they decided that earth needed a defense against all extraterrestrial anomalies and entities.

They started the project 7 months later after the foundation contained SCP-2845 and finished it 4 years later with the help of Anderson’s Robotics.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the hook here is about how the foundation is supposed to take control of the space cannon program from the GOC and the problem with fragments of the ship being used by civilians and groups of interest, like Anderson’s Robotics experimenting with SCP-XXXX-2 or the chaos Insurgency using it as a powerful weapon/bomb.

Additional Notes: this SCP idea is split up in 2 forms, 1 being about the SCP itself and 1 about Project Space Cannon and why the GOC built it, there is also going to be a series of events that took place in the ship before its doom, the trouble of keeping this from the public and a series of test involving SCP-XXXX-2.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there EnderDragon101. Let’s take a look at your concept.

Overall, I agree with Quadraginta’s assessment: the concept sounds too ambitious, with you including multiple anomalies with little to no explanation as to their purpose or intention.

Mind you, it’s not about whether the concept is heavily sci-fi or not. It’s what you do with the many elements you’ve cited. What does the GOC have to do shooting down an alien ship, for example? What does “Galactic.Co” have to do with the alien’s purpose for being on earth? Why cross a human with an orca to make the alien? Is it just to make them look/sound cool? Finally, the whole description of SCP-xxxx-2 and SCP-xxxx-3 is overly confusing. It’s not clear why you needed to have two different materials in the first place, and what their significance is to the Foundation or the GOC.

The danger of picking a sci-fi setting is most beginning authors feel that they can get away with including multiple out-of-this-world / bizarre concepts and then make the excuse that “Oh, it’s just because it’s sci-fi” for their existence. Sorry, but the base rules of storytelling still apply: tell us what’s happening in your Central Narrative segment, and ensure that all the elements are clearly linked together. A majority of your Central Narrative atm is simply describing the SCP, and not going into enough detail about the actual narrative.

I hope you continue working on the concept though. The strength of a sci-fi concept is that you can really think out of the box, but some restraint is needed here. If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. Best of luck!

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
PM request. Placeholder.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Never thought that the GOC could declare war on 85% of the Milky Way Galaxy, but man were we wrong.

Immediately, you have my attention, but I'm not sure if it's in a good way or bad way.

Generally, a first SCP shouldn't be too ambitious or grand, as all that ambition can come crashing right back down on you.

I do speak from experience.

SCP-XXXX/2 are monoliths that contains SCP-XXXX/3 which is gravitonium, SCP-XXXX/2 is made of an unknown element never seen before but are considered safe, SCP-XXXX/3 on the other hand is highly dangerous and is considered unpredictable, SCP-XXXX/3 has the ability to manipulate gravity which can result in casualties.

At first, I was a bit confused by the wording; I thought SCP-XXXX-2 (that's the proper formatting btw) was made of SCP-XXXX-3, but then it occurred to me that it was just the container.

Overall, you got some interesting bits, but it feels like the start to a generic sci-fi/science fantasy space war story.

I don't really see why the GoC would just declare war like that on 85% of the milky way galaxy? If anything, I see the orca-humanoids declaring war on the GoC since they blew up their ship.

The Foundation pacifically one of the O5 counsel could gain a seat in the galactic senate allowing the foundation to have an influence on the galaxy.

Foundation lore is entirely up to headcanon since no Canon exists, and this may be just me, but I'm not sure if people would buy having the Foundation not already be well versed in galactic level anomalies happening; there are plenty of other interstellar SCPs and you'd have to think of some damn fine reasoning for why they'd want to team up with some random new orca-humanoids.

If anything, I see them confiscating the gravitonium and containing the survivors.

The second being the Capital Planet which have a strong government, a strong military and controls 85% of the entire galaxy, The Capital Planet could be a new Group of Interest sense they share some of the same goals, to protect humanity even though the Capital actually protects all underdeveloped civilizations,

This definitely feels like generic sci-fi world building.

Granted, I admit I'm not the best person to seek out for sci-fi critique.

All in all, I'm sorry, but I'm not feeling this. It feels like generic sci-fi, space fantasy space warfare and it also feels way too ambitious for a first SCP, as weird of a critique as that may be.

Though, if you do seek to pursue this, then feel free to reach out to someone in the butterfly squad roster. There is definitely someone there who can help with sci-fi. Right off the top of my head, I believe caspian2 is good with that genre.

Regardless, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day. 👍

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: never thought the GOC is heartless enough to shoot down an innocent alien cargo ship, but man were we wrong.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is an alien cargo ship that was shot down by the GOC and crashed 20 miles west of San Francisco, pieces of the SCP-XXXX was too badly damaged to know the original shape or size of it, but a name was discovered “Galactic.Co”

SCP-XXXX-1 is the Survivors of the incident and appears to be a combination of a human and a orca, they are strong, intelligent and can swim very fast, but because of the GOC they are stuck here with no way for them to contact their home world, but they are cooperative.

SCP-XXXX-2 are monoliths that contains SCP-XXXX-3 which is gravitonium, SCP-XXXX-2 is made of an unknown element never seen before but are considered safe, SCP-XXXX-3 on the other hand is highly dangerous and is considered unpredictable, SCP-XXXX-3 has the ability to manipulate gravity which can result in casualties, but it is also useful because of its ability to make artificial gravity and SCP-XXXX-2 is the only thing capable of containing it.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: there’s 3 Hooks with this SCP idea.

The first being SCP-XXXX-3 the gravitonium, if the Foundation managed to create an SCP-XXXX-2 then they would be able to use SCP-XXXX-3 for artificial gravity, this SCP could change the Foundation in the near future if successfully contained and controlled.

The second is because some of SCP-XXXX-2 with SCP-XXXX-3 was sucked out and landing in places where there’s more of SCP-XXXX-3 underground and worse where GoI are digging them up, fortunately only the foundation has the SCP-XXXX-2’s.

And the third is the idea of whether or not the SCP-XXXX/1’s are ever going to see home again or if the GOC finds out about them, how would they react.

Additional Notes: this SCP idea is split up in 2 forms, 1 being about the SCP itself and 1 about Project Space Cannon and why the GOC built it, there is also going to be a series of events that took place in the ship before its doom, the trouble of keeping this from the public and a series of test involving SCP-XXXX-2 and 3.
